problem_decription:
Spring Boot, React and MySQL: Electronics Gadgets Store ApplicationObjectiveThis project aims to create an application for an electronics dealer to manage their gadget inventory.Develop a user-friendly application to:Maintain a list of electronic gadgets offered by the store.Display individual gadget details with all details.Allow users to navigate between gadget overview and detailed views.Backend: Electronics Gadget APIImplement REST APIs to list all the gadget's data and also retrieve a specific gadget by ID from the collection of the Gadgets.The Gadgets entity should have the following attributes:id: the unique id of the gadget (Integer)itemName: the name of the gadget (String)brandName: the brand name of the gadget (String)units: the number of units available (Integer)price: the price of the gadgets per unit (Float)Here is an example of a Gadgets JSON object:[
    {
        "id": 1,
        "itemName": "Mobile",
        "brandName": "Vivo",
        "units": 5,
        "price": 13000.0
    },
    {
        "id": 2,
        "itemName": "Washing Machine",
        "brandName": "LG",
        "units": 3,
        "price": 15000.0
    }
]
You are provided with the implementation of the models required for all the APIs. Your task is to implement a set of REST services that exposes the endpoints and allows for listing all the gadgets and listing one gadget based on the ID.| API Route               | API Type | Success Response Code  | Validation Error Code  |
|-------------------------|----------|------------------------|------------------------|
| /gadgets                | GET      | 200                    | 404                    |
| /gadgets/{gadgetsId}    | GET      | 200                    | 404                    |
Task 1: Service Layer Implementation in GadgetsServiceImplement the business logic in the service layer using GadgetsRepositoryMethod Details:getAllItems(): Implement the GET method which should list all the gadgets.getItemsById(): Implement the GET method which should list a gadget by ID.Task 2: REST API Endpoints in GadgetsControllerGET request to /gadgetsReturn a collection of all the gadgetsResponse Body: JSON object representing the gadgets details.HTTP Status Code:200 (OK) - If the details of all the gadgets are found404 (Not Found) - If there are no such gadgetsGET request to /gadgets/{gadgetsId}Return a single gadget based on the gadgetsIdResponse Body: JSON object representing the details of a gadget.HTTP Status Code:200 (OK) - If the details of the requested gadgetsId are found404 (Not Found) - If there is no such gadget for the given gadgetsIdComplete the given project so that it passes all the test cases when running the provided unit tests.Example Requests and Responses:GET request to /gadgets:The response code is 200 and the response body, when converted to JSON, is as follows:[
	{
    	"id": 1,
    	"itemName": "Mobile",
    	"brandName": "Vivo",
    	"units": 5,
    	"price": 13000.0
	},
	{
    	"id": 2,
    	"itemName": "Washing Machine",
    	"brandName": "LG",
    	"units": 3,
    	"price": 15000.0
	}
]
GET request to /gadgets/{gadgetsId}:The response code is 200 and the response body, when converted to JSON, is as follows:{
	"id": 1,
	"itemName": "Mobile",
	"brandName": "Vivo",
	"units": 5,
	"price": 13000.0
}
Frontend: Electronics Gadget ApplicationUIComponentsThe application consists of four primary components:GadgetShowCase:Fetches a list of gadgets from the server using a GET request to {apiUrl}gadgets.Stores the retrieved data as an array in the component's state.Iterates through the gadget array and renders each gadget using the GadgetCard component.Each gadget card is clickable and routes to the detailed view (/gadgets/{id}) upon click, where id is the specific gadget's ID.Renders on the application's root path (/).Assigns a unique data-testid attribute (gadgetcard-{id}) to each gadget card for testing purposes.GadgetCard:Presents essential gadget details within the user interface.Includes a h1 tag with data-testid="title-{id} displaying the brand name and item name separated by a space.Features a h3 tag with data-testid="price-{id} showcasing the gadget's price.Integrates data test IDs for effective component testing.GadgetDetailsWrapper:A functional component responsible for rendering on the /gadget/:id route.Extracts the gadget ID from the URL parameters.Passes the extracted ID as a prop to the GadgetDetails component.GadgetDetails:Retrieves detailed information for a specific gadget using a GET request to {apiUrl}gadgets/{id}.Displays the fetched data in the following format:Header with data-testid="header" displaying "brandName itemName".h3 elements with designated data test IDs ("price", "units", "brand", "category") showcasing the gadget's price, units available, brand, and category, respectively.A link with data-testid="goBackBtn" facilitating navigation back to the gadget overview (/).RoutingRouting logic is implemented within the App.js component.TestingData test IDs (data-testid) are crucial for ensuring component functionality through automated testing.Expected Live PreviewCommandsInstall Packages & Build Backend::cd $HOME/$NAME/backend && mvn clean install -DskipTests
This command would run automatically when the IDE loads, however, if there is some issue, you may have to run it manually.Start Backend API Server:cd $HOME/$NAME/backend && mvn clean spring-boot:run -DskipTests
This command will start the server.Once the server is started, navigate to the Thunder Client's tab  and click on New Request.Test the API endpoints by sending specific requests to http://localhost:8000/{endpoints}. You can view the JSON response in the "Response" tab.Run Backend Test Cases:cd $HOME/$NAME/backend && mvn clean test
This will run the test cases in the terminal.Install Frontend Packages:cd $HOME/$NAME/frontend && npm install
This command would run automatically when the IDE loads, however if there is some issue, you may have to run it manually.Start Frontend Dev Server:cd $HOME/$NAME/frontend && npm start
This command will start the dev server. You can view the Live Preview once the server is started in multiple ways:Click the Preview in Editor option that pops up at the bottom-right cornerClick the Open Preview option in the Run menuRun Frontend Test Cases:cd $HOME/$NAME/frontend && npm test
This will run the frontend test cases in the terminal.These commands can be executed in the terminal or by selecting options from the Run menu.EnvironmentReact Version: 18.2.0Java version: 11Maven version: 3.6.3Spring Boot version: 2.6.1Frontend Default Port: 3000Backend Default Port: 8000
